The application stands disposed of.

This is a petition seeking quashing of the FIR No. 42/2022 dated 04.05.2022 registered under Section 420 IPC read with Section 120B IPC at PS Cyber Police Station (South) and charge sheet dated 24.11.2022 bearing No. 73/2022 as well as unfreezing of bank accounts.
2. Along with the petition, the petitioners have also sought quashing of the summon/ warrant dated 23.02.2023 against the petitioner No.5.

sentences.text: The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 20:42:15 3.
The allegations in the FIR are that the petitioners hacked the account of Paytel Financial Technologies Pvt. Ltd. and made multiple fraudulent transactions to withdraw money from their accounts.
Hence, the FIR.

4. During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement dated 11.05.2023, wherein the parties have settled their disputes and the petitioners have made a payment of Rs. 9.85 lakhs to the respondent No.2.
5.

It is stated by Mr. Kshirsagar, learned counsel for the petitioner that without going into the allegations in the FIR or the charge sheet, the petitioners were not at fault and have compromised the disputes only to avoid further involvement in criminal proceedings.

6. Petitioner Nos. 1 to 3 are present in Court and petitioner Nos. 4 and 5 have joined through video conferencing mode and they all have been identified by Mr. Mayank Kshirsagar, learned counsel.
7.
The respondent No.2 has also joined through video conferencing mode and has been identified by Ms. Shrishti Govil, learned counsel.
8. The parties state that they have arrived at the aforesaid settlement out of their own free will and without any undue influence, threat, pressure or coercion.
9. The respondent No.2 states that he has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
10. In the present case, there are no other criminal antecedents of the petitioners.
11. However, in the present case, the FIR is of the year 2022 and the charge sheet has been filed after investigation.
Not only the Police have investigated the entire matter but also considerable time of the police as This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 20:42:15 well as judicial time has been wasted which could have been utilised for important matters has been misdirected towards this case.
Even though the parties have settled their disputes and quashing will put a quietus to the matter, I am of the view that petitioners must pay some costs.

12. Since all the petitioners are college students and have no other criminal antecedents as well as no other case pending against them, each of the petitioners shall deposit Rs. 2,500/- with DSLSA within 2 weeks from today.

13. Subject to the above, the FIR No. 42/2022 dated 04.05.2022 registered under Section 420 IPC read with Section 120B IPC at PS Cyber Police Station (South) and charge sheet dated 24.11.2022 bearing No. 73/2022 as well as all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby Nikhil Girish Pise And Ors vs State N C T Of Delhi And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24328581/
2 quashed.
14.
